assertions.description: RTCPeerConnection.startDiagnosticLogging is a static function — the current WICG draft's IDL location for beginning a session (Chrome 151's origin trial instead binds navigator.rtc, so this can honestly fail there).
RTCPeerConnection.finishDiagnosticLogging is a static function — finalises the local log, accepting RTCFinishDiagnosticLoggingOptions with closing metadata.
RTCPeerConnection.cancelDiagnosticLogging is a static function — discards the captured data.

The API is exposed through at least one known binding: the spec draft's RTCPeerConnection statics or Chrome 151's origin-trial navigator.rtc interface (Chromium navigator_rtc.idl, RuntimeEnabled=RTCDiagnosticLogging).
assertions.test: (() => { const viaPc = typeof RTCPeerConnection !== 'undefined' && typeof RTCPeerConnection.startDiagnosticLogging === 'function' && typeof RTCPeerConnection.finishDiagnosticLogging === 'function' && typeof RTCPeerConnection.cancelDiagnosticLogging === 'function'; const viaNav = !!navigator.rtc && typeof navigator.rtc.startDiagnosticLogging === 'function' && typeof navigator.rtc.finishDiagnosticLogging === 'function' && typeof navigator.rtc.cancelDiagnosticLogging === 'function'; return viaPc || viaNav; })()

assertions.description: The interface is [SecureContext]: on a non-secure context neither navigator.rtc nor the RTCPeerConnection diagnostic statics may be present (on a secure context either state is spec-legal, since the runtime feature also gates exposure).
assertions.test: (() => { const anyBinding = !!navigator.rtc || (typeof RTCPeerConnection !== 'undefined' && typeof RTCPeerConnection.startDiagnosticLogging === 'function'); return window.isSecureContext ? true : !anyBinding; })()

assertions.description: Wherever the API is bound, startDiagnosticLogging() with 6 metadata entries rejects before any recording starts (the spec mandates TypeError; Chromium main currently rejects with RangeError — rtc.cc RejectWithRangeError — so either name proves enforcement).
assertions.test: (async () => { const b = (navigator.rtc && typeof navigator.rtc.startDiagnosticLogging === 'function') ? navigator.rtc : ((typeof RTCPeerConnection !== 'undefined' && typeof RTCPeerConnection.startDiagnosticLogging === 'function') ? RTCPeerConnection : null); if (!b) return false; const m = {}; for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) m['k' + i] = 'v'; try { await b.startDiagnosticLogging({ metadata: m }); return false; } catch (e) { return !!e && (e.name === 'TypeError' || e.name === 'RangeError'); } })()

assertions.description: Wherever the API is bound, startDiagnosticLogging() with a metadata value over 100 characters rejects before any recording starts (spec: TypeError; Chromium main: RangeError, measuring UTF-8 bytes — either name proves enforcement).
assertions.test: (async () => { const b = (navigator.rtc && typeof navigator.rtc.startDiagnosticLogging === 'function') ? navigator.rtc : ((typeof RTCPeerConnection !== 'undefined' && typeof RTCPeerConnection.startDiagnosticLogging === 'function') ? RTCPeerConnection : null); if (!b) return false; try { await b.startDiagnosticLogging({ metadata: { app: 'x'.repeat(101) } }); return false; } catch (e) { return !!e && (e.name === 'TypeError' || e.name === 'RangeError'); } })()

assertions.description: finishDiagnosticLogging() accepts RTCFinishDiagnosticLoggingOptions and validates its metadata by the same limits: an over-limit closing metadata value rejects (spec: TypeError; Chromium main: RangeError) without needing an active session, since validation precedes dispatch.
assertions.test: (async () => { const b = (navigator.rtc && typeof navigator.rtc.finishDiagnosticLogging === 'function') ? navigator.rtc : ((typeof RTCPeerConnection !== 'undefined' && typeof RTCPeerConnection.finishDiagnosticLogging === 'function') ? RTCPeerConnection : null); if (!b) return false; try { await b.finishDiagnosticLogging({ metadata: { outcome: 'x'.repeat(101) } }); return false; } catch (e) { return !!e && (e.name === 'TypeError' || e.name === 'RangeError'); } })()
